subject: Quantable Order Form — Clarifying Output & Training Rights
messages:
From: Erin Soto <erin.soto@quantable.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@quantable.com>, legal@quantable.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quantable Order Form v3 — IP & Training redlines

Hi Marcus,

Attached are our redlines to the Order Form + exhibit A. Legal flagged a few items we need clarified before procurement will sign:

- Output ownership: we want explicit assignment (or exclusive license) to productize outputs generated by our data.
- Training/data use: we require an opt-out mechanism so our data/outputs are not used to retrain models used by other customers unless explicitly agreed.
- Feedback: would like a limited license for Redwood to use our feedback to improve the service but only in an aggregated/anonymized way; no attribution.

I attached a PDF with inline comments (Quantable_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf). Can you confirm Redwood's stance and suggest language we can present to our procurement? We're targeting a procurement review on Monday.

Thanks,
Erin Soto
Sr. Procurement Manager
Quantable, Inc.

-----
Attachment: Quantable_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf (annotations)

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quantable Order Form v3 — IP & Training redlines

Hi Erin — thanks for the clear set of asks and the annotated PDF. Looping in Legal (Laura, Olga) to align on workable redline language and internal approvals. A few quick notes from the product/sales side:

- Output ownership: Redwood's standard position is we do not assign ownership of model outputs back to customers as a blanket assignment because outputs are transient and often derivative of both customer data and model pre-training. We can, however, grant a strong, perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive license to the Customer to use, reproduce and distribute Customer Outputs for their productization needs. For customers who need exclusivity, we typically evaluate on a case-by-case commercial basis.

- Training / retrain: we can commit to not using Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train or fine-tune foundation models that are shared with other customers unless the customer explicitly opts in via the Order Form (checkbox + exhibit).

- Feedback license: we can offer a limited, anonymized feedback license allowing Redwood to improve the service (bugs, product features, anonymized telemetry). We should avoid any broad license that would allow building competing models from Customer Outputs.

Next steps: Laura/Olga, can you review and propose redline snippets that I can send back to Erin today? Erin — would a 30-minute sync this afternoon (4pm PT) work to walk through the tradeoffs?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Erin Soto <erin.soto@quantable.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quantable Order Form v3 — proposed redline language

Marcus / Olga — below is suggested language we can propose back to Quantable. Kept it narrow and operational, avoids assignment language while giving Quantable the rights they need to productize. Please review and flag any product or commercial objections.

Suggested redline snippets (to include in Order Form / Exhibit A):

1) Customer Output License
"Customer shall own the Customer Data. For Output generated by the Service using Customer Data (\"Customer Output\"), Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive right and license to use, reproduce, distribute, and create Derivative Works of Customer Output for Customer's internal business purposes and for productization of Customer's own offerings. Redwood expressly disclaims assignment of title to any underlying models or model weights."

2) Training / Model Use
"Redwood will not use Customer Data or Customer Output to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any models that are then used to provide service to other customers without Customer's prior written opt-in. Customer may elect to opt-in to specific training programs by checking the corresponding box in Exhibit A and by executing a separate Data Use Addendum. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may use anonymized and aggregated telemetry for service stability and security purposes."

3) Feedback License
"Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use Feedback (as defined in the Agreement) solely to operate, maintain, and improve the Service; provided that such use will be in aggregated, anonymized form and shall not include attribution to Customer or disclosure of Customer Confidential Information."

Operational notes: add an explicit checkbox section in Exhibit A ("Training Opt-In") and a short definition table for Customer Output vs. Customer Confidential Information. Also recommend procurement accept a narrow Productization license rather than assignment — faster approval cycle.

Marcus: if Sales is comfortable with the non-exclusive productization license above, we can return this language and propose the training opt-in workflow in Exhibit A. If Quantable insists on assignment language, we should escalate to commercial leadership and prepare a priced exclusivity option.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
